description: I AM SARTHAK YADAV IN FIRST YEAR BCA DATA SCIENCE
summary: Project RESONA is an open, offline-capable web observatory for exploring sunlight and Earth communication windows at candidate lunar South Pole landing sites. Near the lunar poles, the Sun circles the horizon at shallow angles while Earth hovers above the northern rim, nodding slowly with lunar libration. Even small crater ridges cast long shadows and block direct radio contact. RESONA visualizes both bodies together against a 360° horizon profile and pairs the sky view with a synchronized three-track timeline showing solar power, Earth link, and their overlapping "resonance" windows across an entire 8,760-hour year. Mission planners can compare two or three sites side by side, test arrival delays, filter candidates by power and blackout limits, and export CSV or print reports. Educators and the public can switch to guided story steps, plain-language captions, and optional audio sonification to hear orbital alignment.
details:
• What it does: Renders an interactive lunar South Pole horizon silhouette alongside a high-speed canvas timeline of solar illumination (Power), Earth direct line-of-sight (Link), and simultaneous overlap (Resonance), plus a 2–3 site comparison workspace with mission constraint filtering and CSV/URL/print export.
  • How it works: Computes hourly Sun and Earth azimuth/elevation angles over 8,760 hours using lunar synodic (29.5306 d), sidereal (27.3217 d), and anomalistic (27.5546 d) harmonic periods and 1.5424° axial obliquity, masks them against a 1°-sampled horizon elevation profile (-0.1° solar upper-limb grazing threshold; 0.0° Earth RF clearance), compresses hourly flags into Run-Length Encoded (RLERun[]) intervals, and evaluates mission thresholds in O(runs) time. Custom lat/lon coordinates execute in a WebGPU compute shader or Web Worker fallback.
  • Benefits & Intended Impact: Unifies power and telecom planning in one intuitive spatial-temporal view, lowers the barrier for students and citizens to understand polar lunar geometry, and operates completely offline in the field via PWA caching.
  • Tools Used: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 2D Canvas, Web Audio API, WebGPU / Web Workers, WebXR (optional), Workbox PWA, Node.js test runner.
  • Creativity & Factors Considered: Horizon-first panoramic framing; "entangled scrubbing" and catenary filaments as a visual progress cue; consonant fifth vs. unresolved interval sonification for accessibility and insight; lunar libration (±6.7° lat / ±7.8° lon), terrain masking, DEM resolution limits, WCAG 2.1 AA contrast/non-color patterns, and reduced-motion support.
